about: Shared consumer-rule cases. release-compat's checkInstall, station_cli's catalog, the kiosk's CompatibilityData and install.sh's jq rule must all give `installable` for every case. A case's `channel` (production | development) is the channel of the installing station: floors are read from requires[Y].channels[channel]; no `channel`, or a requirement without `channels`, uses the top-level floor. Cutover: components[X].enforced_from (a tag, or null = every release legacy) splits releases into LEGACY (version < it) and ENFORCED; a component without the key (the `synthetic` doc) is read by the classic rule. A LEGACY candidate gets no computed constraint on a pair when it has no evidence on that edge (no requires[Y] for the channel, or one that tested nothing) or the installed release is legacy without evidence on it (requires[X]); it is then installable as far as the file goes and the consumer applies the legacy rule (metadata keys) to that pair; a legacy candidate not in the file is installable that way. An ENFORCED candidate must be in the file with a floor for every edge of its component (installed or not) and passes the full rule. Copy this file verbatim; the source of truth is release-compat/test/fixtures/consumer-parity.json.
